text:
The Mammoth are running out of forwards. Logan Cooley is out, Nick Schmaltz hurt his lower body against Vegas, and Dylan Guenther is on injured reserve for two to four weeks. Cooley had 13 points in his last ten games before he went down, so this isn't depth they're missing.

Utah is winless in five (0-2-3), outscored 21-14, and in that stretch the chances are on the other side, 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). The Athletic's Jesse Granger called Saturday's 5-3 Vegas win impressive even with Utah missing several stars. At 10-8-3 with 23 points, the Mammoth still have 67% playoff odds by our numbers.

Over the full season, the play has been much better than the record. Utah has taken 57% of the five-on-five expected goals, and our points model has them almost three points behind what their play has earned. The goaltending is the gap: almost 11 goals more allowed than the chances would usually produce. Sebastian Cossa is at .869 and 4.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. The MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev pair has 57% of the chances and has still been outscored 13-6.

Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton have taken 74% of the chances together. What we'd watch: André Tourigny's lineup until the injured return, and whether Cossa steadies.
